page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.48xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 192 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARM64 architecture, specifically the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 model running at 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It includes 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps, all running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data highlights top-tier multi-core performance and memory throughput. The instance achieves top-tier status in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth tests, reaching 895.63 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 411.52 GB/sec for uncached large-block writes. Single-core performance sits in the average tier, as shown by stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core results. The server excels in database operations, scoring in the top tier for Passmark database operations and delivering 361.71 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks.

Given its high resource density, the r8gd.48xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring massive memory footprints and high-speed local storage without the overhead of external network storage. The combination of 192 dedicated ARM64 cores, 1.5 TB of RAM, and 11.4 TB of local NVMe SSD makes this instance highly suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, high-throughput Redis deployments, data-intensive web serving, and software compilation pipelines.
